# optimizelycmp_webhook (Resource)

A webhook, written through the API's bulk settings import (experimental). The import matches by name and never deletes, so: event names can be added but not removed (the plan fails if you try), the name cannot change (a new name is a new webhook), and destroying this resource only stops Terraform managing it. The API returns the secret in full, so it is stored in state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "webhook_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "optimizelycmp_webhook" "tasks" {
  name         = "Task events"
  description  = "Sends task events to our service"
  callback_url = "https://hooks.example.com/cmp"
  secret       = var.webhook_secret

  # Events can be added but never removed.
  event_names = ["task_added", "task_modified", "task_removed"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `callback_url` (String) URL CMP calls. Must be https.
- `event_names` (Set of String) Events to subscribe to. The settings import only accepted these when tested: asset_added, asset_modified, asset_removed, external_sub_step_comment_added/modified/removed, external_sub_step_completed/modified/started, task_asset_added/modified/removed, task_asset_draft_added/removed, task_brief_added/modified/removed, task_custom_field_modified, task_metadata_modified and task_removed. It rejects others that exist in CMP (such as task_added or work_request_added). Events can be added but not removed.
- `name` (String) Webhook name. Changing it creates a new webhook and leaves the old one in CMP.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Secret CMP uses to sign calls. It is stored in Terraform state; prefer a variable or secret store over writing it in configuration.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The webhook name (the API gives webhooks no other identifier).
